new_statements.relation_note: Agrees with the catalog penultimate stress (penultimate) and adds the domain (stress assigned after suffixation, before final [-a] epenthesis, so many surface forms look antepenultimate), the two lexical exceptions, and the stress-retracted -na noun form.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the word as it stands after suffixation but before the word-final epenthetic vowel [-a] is added to consonant-final stems; surface antepenultimate stress in words like ['yabana] 'sky' and [a'bagala] 'I erred' is therefore penultimate at the stage where stress is assigned. Stress moves rightward with each suffix ([a'xabi] ~ [axa'bidi]; [axalu'vila] ~ [axaluvi'lamna] ~ [axaluvilem'nei]).
new_statements.exceptions: Two lexical exceptions (p. 269): /a-bobuala/ [a'bobwara] 'I talk' and /a-uiauana/ [au'yawana] 'I rejoice' have antepenultimate stress in the intransitive form although the stem is not consonant-final (no epenthesis), 'These are the only exceptions that have been found.' Separately, section 4.4 (pp. 313-314): inalienably possessed nouns in the neutralised form with invariant -na take 'a shift in stress one syllable to the left' ([ma'ta-gu] vs ['matana] 'eye', [da'ba-gu] vs ['dabana] 'head', ['nimana] 'hand'), i.e. antepenultimate/initial stress in that construction. Section 2.1.5 (p. 258): /a/ is [ə] in unstressed syllables.
new_statements.identity_note: Olson describes Gumawana as spoken in the Amphlett Islands, Milne Bay Province (the SIL OPD calls it 'Gumawana (Gumasi)', ISO gvs); no dialect split is discussed. The listed SIL OPD (Olson 1992, Ukarumpa) is by the same author as the opened Pacific Linguistics sketch and almost certainly restates the same penultimate rule, but that was not verified because the OPD could not be opened.

new_statements.quote: Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length) Length: Stressed syllables are lengthened to indicate intensity: niyala [...] 'sun', niiyala [...] 'very hot sun'. Vowel lengthening in the penultimate syllable from the stressed syllable is used to indicate imperfective aspect in verbs and in derived adjectives: atusobu 'I sat, sit down', aatusobu 'I am sitting', maavadaina 'pure'. [...] Transitional [j] and [w] are written word internally but not over morpheme boundaries: ietune [i je’tune] 'he sent it' , kuetune [ku we’tune] 'you sent it'.

new_statements.relation_note: Catalog records penultimate stress (penultimate stress). The OPD states no placement rule, but everything it shows (a single stressed syllable per word; stress marks on the penult in [je'tune], [we'tune]) is consistent with the catalog's fixed: penultimate syllable record; it adds only the length facts (emphatic lengthening of the stressed syllable; aspectual pre-stress vowel lengthening), not a different placement. new_statements.rule_in_words: The OPD does not state a stress-placement rule in words. Its Suprasegmentals section presupposes one stressed syllable per word (stressed syllables lengthen for intensity; imperfective aspect is marked by lengthening a vowel located relative to the stressed syllable) and gives no tone statement. The only placement evidence is incidental: the two stress-marked phonetic forms [i je'tune] 'he sent it' and [ku we'tune] 'you sent it' (i.e.tu.ne, ku.e.tu.ne) carry the stress mark before the penultimate syllable, consistent with penultimate stress.
new_statements.exceptions: None in the OPD. (The fuller companion source already held by the project, Olson 1992 PL A-82 section 2.5 pp. 268-269, states 'With a few exceptions, stress falls on the penultimate syllable', with apparent antepenultimate cases explained by stress assignment before epenthetic final [-a], and two lexical exceptions a-bobuala 'I talk', a-uiauana 'I rejoice'; that work is not in this item's list and is cited here only for context.)
new_statements.identity_note: The OPD covers Gumawana (Gumasi) [GVS] of the Amphlett Islands (villages Gumawana, Nubogeta, Kotoita, Omea, Bituma), Esa'ala district, Milne Bay Province; data checked by Cliff Olson, September 1992. Same variety as the catalog entry.
